selected.title: OpenAI prompt-to-voice creates reusable voices for GPT-Live agents
selected.summary: OpenAI made prompt-to-voice generally available to API customers. Builders can create and save an adult synthetic voice from a text description, then use its voice ID in GPT-Live.
selected.availability: Available to API customers through POST /v1/audio/voices. Prompt-generated voices work with GPT-Live only, with up to 100 prompt-generated voices per organization.
selected.practical_use: Define a consistent adult voice for a support or onboarding agent, save the returned voice ID, add the original description to the GPT-Live session instructions, and evaluate it with a fixed script and conversation turns.

source_review.excerpt: Prompt-to-voice lets you create a new voice from a text description.
source_review.decision: Read the October 16 API changelog and full custom-voices guide. This is a documented walkthrough; AI Daily Diff did not create a voice or run GPT-Live.
source_review.availability: GA for API customers. Prompt-generated voices are limited to GPT-Live, billed through GPT-Live speech use, and the voice-creation endpoint is not compatible with Zero Data Retention.

openai.reason: OpenAI's October 16 changelog and custom-voices guide document prompt-to-voice for all API customers and its GPT-Live-only boundary.

anthropic.reason: The official newsroom had no newer model or product capability after the October 14 items relevant to this run.

google.reason: The latest material model release is Gemini 4 Argon from October 13, already covered by episode 2026-10-15-gemini-argon-api.

repositories.reason: Anthropic's October 17 agent security review cookbook is a strong repository lead, but it needs a separate runnable review of the notebook and rules before publication.

architectures.reason: ARIA is an October 14 research-only architecture for runtime inspection and repair of multi-agent systems; its method and reported dataset need a dedicated Deep review.

editorial_review.context: agents / builder / daily; OpenAI prompt-to-voice release on October 16
editorial_review.viewer_question: How can a builder create a consistent synthetic voice for a GPT-Live agent, and what limits must be designed around?
editorial_review.prerequisites: An OpenAI API project, GPT-Live access, an adult synthetic voice concept and a fixed evaluation script.
editorial_review.central_task: Create and save one prompt-generated voice, attach its ID to a GPT-Live session, and evaluate consistency with a fixed script and conversation turns.
editorial_review.new_capability: API customers can create reusable voices from text descriptions without a reference or consent recording, then use them in GPT-Live.
editorial_review.closest_archive_coverage: All episode files and confirmed receipts reviewed through October 15; no prior custom-voice or GPT-Live prompt-to-voice episode.
editorial_review.supported_payoff: A builder can give a voice agent a repeatable, project-specific speaking style and validate it before deployment.
editorial_review.evidence_mode_reason: Documented API and workflow review; no live voice creation, listening test or GPT-Live session by AI Daily Diff.
editorial_review.alternatives: The Anthropic agent security review cookbook is newer but needs artifact testing; ARIA is research-only; Gemini Argon is already covered.
editorial_review.selection_rationale: The release is recent, generally available, primary-sourced and supports a concrete builder workflow with explicit safety and platform limits.
editorial_review.search_query: OpenAI prompt-to-voice GPT-Live custom voice API
editorial_review.final_verdict: The viewer learns a new way to create a reusable GPT-Live voice, the exact first integration steps and every material access and safety boundary.
editorial_review.metadata_review: Title and description name prompt-to-voice, GPT-Live and the builder task. Availability, safety, billing and no-live-test wording match the script.
editorial_review.useful_example: Create one disclosed adult onboarding voice, attach its ID to a GPT-Live session, then review a fixed script and conversational turns.
editorial_review.availability_limitation: GPT-Live only; 100 prompt-generated voices per organization; no ZDR for creation; generated voices are not guaranteed unique.
editorial_review.accept_reject_rationale: Accepted as a recent, broadly available agent-building capability with a concrete implementation path and distinct archive coverage.

playlist_review.reason: The complete episode answers one builder workflow question: how to create, attach and evaluate a reusable voice for a GPT-Live agent while preserving disclosure and platform limits. Every segment fits the agents playlist.
